qualification_scope: Bounded CPU executor and integrated animation/material/profiler correctness, actual preserved compiled gameplay, original Vulkan poses and synthetic CPU timing. No whole-game FPS, physical input, GUI, general parallel physics/AI or production-platform claim.

sanitizers.notes: ASan+UBSan and TSan scheduler15/profiler5 groups pass. No runtime reports or suppressions; recorded profiler compile logs retain existing malloc/free test allocator warnings.

documentation.installed_client: Fresh virtual environment; pip install ./tools/python, no PYTHONPATH

method.comparison: Six contexts run the same fixed ticks; mode order rotates each tick. This reduces but does not eliminate cache, scheduling or thermal bias.
method.cpu_time: Not measured; no wall-time-to-CPU utilization inference
method.excluded: fixture/context/pool construction, pose serialization/byte comparison/hashing, final save_state serialization, reporting, separate optional profiler run
method.limits: Original synthetic CPU-only animation workload. No GPU, whole-game FPS, real asset throughput, laptop frame-budget or guaranteed speedup claim.
method.memory: Process aggregate across six simultaneously live contexts and15 idle worker threads; lifetime peak is not isolated per-mode or per-workload memory. Includes verification buffers.
method.pose_hash: SHA256 of the ordered newline-terminated per-tick SHA256 hex hashes of entity IDs and little-endian IEEE-double local TRS field bytes; all modes additionally compare actual field bytes each tick
method.sampling_scope: RuntimeAnimations::sample: candidate copies, per-rig TRS/layer/inertial evaluation, scheduling, wait, flattening and owner commit
method.total_scope: bounded command generation/application plus sampling for one fixed tick

windows.execution_context: All owned compiler, managed-build, sanitizer and Vulkan correctness workloads had ended before timing. Ordinary OS/background activity was not controlled. One run per OS; no performance threshold.

limits: Default owner pools have two workers; 0..8 is explicit policy. Different creating owners have independent budgets. This is not process-wide CPU or memory admission.

Callbacks have bounded scheduler admission; arbitrary capture/output memory and cooperative cancellation duration remain consumer responsibilities. Terminal state fences callback capture cleanup; retained exception handles may live longer.
Animation/math comparisons are exact within the tested host/compiler modes; universal cross-compiler floating-point identity is not established.
Jolt physics, C# gameplay callbacks, authoritative registry, rendering commands and material file publication remain owner-thread operations.
Tracing measures elapsed wall intervals, not sampled on-CPU utilization or presented frame times. GPU clocks remain uncorrelated.
The timing fixture is original CPU-only animation, with six live contexts and 15 mostly idle worker threads. Memory is process aggregate, not isolated per-mode memory.
C# qualification uses existing layers fixtures with matching preserved SDK/bridge/hostfxr and actual .58 Native AOT game artifacts. It is not a clean-machine deployment check.
Vulkan qualification is one GPU and bounded ribbon poses; it does not qualify physical input, the current GUI or production-character appearance.
Playbook qualification runs a same-owner intervening edit, fresh-owner persistence and receipt replay; no provider or unknown-outcome injection is involved.

vulkan_animation.scope: Actual Windows Vulkan animation/layer/inertial ribbon pose correctness only; no game-performance, GUI or physical-input qualification

representative_review.method: Lossless BMP-to-PNG conversion for view_image inspection only; original image untouched.
representative_review.observed: A visible diagonal blue ribbon against the dark background; bounded pose fixture only.
